title: Xanthe and the Choir
premise: Petra Nakamura, runaway apprentice to the hedge-witch Maren, has spent her whole life in the valley where magic cannot cross the boundary stones — the only safe place left. When a feral child named Xanthe arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Petra discovers the valley's protection is failing: a parasitic crown-spirit has been consuming the memories of the dead king Aldric, and Xanthe is the last vessel of the language that can unbind it. As Petra and Xanthe flee across a land where magic devours the unwary, Petra learns the valley's safety was purchased with her mother's memories — an inheritance of forgetting. In the climax, Petra must surrender her own treasured memories of Maren to complete the unbinding rite as the thirteenth moon rises, freeing King Aldric and breaking the crown's hunger. Xanthe's language dies with the crown, but Petra chooses to carry it forward, teaching the child to speak in new words, and the two return to a valley whose stones now stand open.
about_author: Juniper Coldharbour is the pen name of a former choir librarian who spent a decade cataloguing hymnals in abandoned parish churches across the northern moors. They write fantasy about the things we inherit without being asked — languages, debts, and songs stuck in the head.

chapters.title: The Boundary Stones
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra tends Maren's herb garden and chafes against the valley's stillness, where no spell will light and no memory of the outside world survives the stones. She steals a look at Maren's locked almanac and finds her own mother's name inked out. Beat: restless longing curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: A Knock at Dusk
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. On the eve of the autumn equinox, a mud-caked child appears at the door, speaking in a language that makes Maren drop a full jar of valerian. The child carries a scrap of royal purple and a crown-shaped burn scar on her palm. Maren's face goes grey. Beat: dread arriving on small feet.

chapters.title: What Maren Buried
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Maren confesses the valley's secret: it was warded by Petra's mother, who gave her memories as payment, and the ward is fraying because the crown-thing has found the boundary. Maren orders Petra to hide the child. Petra refuses to be protected twice. Beat: the mentor's authority cracks.

chapters.title: The Language of Before
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra names the child Xanthe and begins mapping her strange tongue, discovering it is not a language but a binding grammar — words that make things true. Xanthe's first true-word heals a dying goat. Petra realizes the crown is hunting Xanthe to silence her. Beat: wonder shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridgeline
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Crown riders in grey livery crest the ridge, led by the serene Chancellor Vey, whose eyes reflect light wrong. They ask politely for a child. Maren lies with her life. Petra flees through the herb tunnels with Xanthe as the house burns behind them. Beat: the safe world ends in smoke.

chapters.title: Crossing the Stones
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the boundary, Petra steps through for the first time in her life — and magic hits her like cold water. Xanthe's true-words blaze. Behind them, Maren stays to hold the ward and does not follow. Petra's grief is immediate and unaffordable. Beat: exile as both wound and liberation.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Outside the valley, roads literally remember everyone who has walked them, replaying footsteps of the dead. Petra learns to read the road and finds her mother's footprints leading toward the capital, years old, never returning. Beat: hope and grief braided together.

chapters.title: The Tinker's Toll
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The tinker Oskar demands payment in memories — a small one, a taste — for passage through his warded wagon. Petra pays a memory of Maren's kitchen and feels the hole where it was. Xanthe watches, learning what memory costs. Beat: the theme made transactional.

chapters.title: Xanthe
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, first in the book. Through Xanthe's eyes we learn she is the last choir-singer of the old tongue, smuggled out of the palace nursery when the crown began eating singers. She is not mute by trauma — she is rationing her words, because every true-word spoken shortens her life. Beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the capital, the court is beautiful and wrong: courtiers repeat conversations from years past, their memories harvested. King Aldric sits the throne with glassy eyes, and when Petra glimpses him, something behind his gaze looks back at her and smiles. Beat: horror wearing velvet.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Vey captures them — but instead of killing Xanthe, offers her sanctuary, revealing the crown-thing does not want the child dead; it wants her voice as its final instrument. Vey genuinely believes eternal, painless memory under the crown is mercy. Beat: an antagonist who is almost right.

chapters.title: The Underchoir
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Escaping Vey's tower through the palace's forgotten crypts, they find the Underchoir — singers who mutilated their own true-words to hide from the crown, now living as ghosts in the dark. Their leader, broken-voiced Sefa, recognizes Xanthe's grammar. Beat: refuge among the ruined.

chapters.title: What Petra's Mother Paid
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the crypt archives, Petra finds her mother's name in the crown's ledger: she was a royal unbinding-rite singer who fled mid-rite, and the valley ward is her unfinished song. Petra's inheritance is not safety but an incomplete obligation. Beat: the theme of inheritance turned knife.

chapters.title: The King in the Garden
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra reaches Aldric alone in the moonlit royal garden, where the crown lets him garden because gardens need no memory. In lucid fragments he begs her — not to save him, but to make sure the thing in the crown does not wear his face forever. Beat: pity before heroism.

chapters.title: Sefa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Underchoir debates: help the girl and the crown will find them, or stay hidden and let it finish eating the kingdom. Sefa, who once sang beside Petra's mother, chooses to give Xanthe the stolen fragments of the unbinding rite — the pieces her generation amputated from themselves. Beat: sacrifice as repair.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Moon
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. With one moon left, the rite requires a choir of true-words and a vessel of willing memory. The Underchoir cannot sing whole; Xanthe cannot sing and live. Petra realizes the rite's missing part is a memory freely given — and her mother's unfinished song is the key. Beat: the trap of the solution.

chapters.title: Vey's Cathedral of Yesterday
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Vey unveils her true project: a cathedral where harvested memories are replayed eternally, a heaven of preserved yesterdays. She offers Petra her mother's memories back — all of them — if she surrenders Xanthe. Petra, aching, nearly says yes. Beat: the temptation that defines her.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra refuses — not because she is noble, but because Xanthe, watching, offers Petra her own last true-word: a memory of Petra's mother, sung once and then gone from Xanthe forever. Receiving it, Petra understands inheritance means passing forward, not hoarding. Beat: the moral heart of the book.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the thirteenth moon, in the cathedral itself, Petra sings her mother's unfinished song, giving her memories of Maren as the willing payment; the Underchoir lends their broken voices; Xanthe spends her words down to near-silence. The crown cracks. Beat: climax — everything paid at once.

chapters.title: The Thing Without a Face
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The crown-spirit, unbound, is a starving hunger older than kingdoms, and it lunges for Xanthe's last word — the only true-word left. Aldric, freed and mortal, throws himself between, and the crown takes him into itself rather than nothing. He dies a king, remembered. Beat: costly victory.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn, New Words
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The kingdom wakes remembering itself, raw and grieving. Vey, her cathedral empty, is left with the mercy she preached and no one to force it on. Xanthe, nearly wordless, begins teaching Petra the grammar by hand-signs, and Petra begins inventing new true-words. Beat: quiet aftermath, grief and beginnings.

chapters.title: Open Stones
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra and Xanthe return to the valley, where Maren survived and the boundary stones stand dark and open — the ward finished at last, no longer needed as a hiding place. Petra plants her mother's herb seeds outside the stones for the first time. Beat: resolution — inheritance carried, not escaped.
